results.title: Together Post-Training: $9/Hour B200 RL and SFT, Explained | explainx.ai Blog | explainx.ai
results.author: Yash Thakker
highlights:
# Together Post-Training: B200s at $9 an Hour, Your Own RL Loop, and a One-Line Tinker Swap

Together Post-Training drops B200 to $9 per GPU-hour for eight weeks, adds MiniMax M3.1 Flash, and lets you write your own SFT or RL loop. What it costs.

Oct 29, 2026· 8 min read· Yash Thakker

Short answer: Together AI's Post-Training service, launched October 19, 2026, lets you write the whole supervised fine-tuning (SFT) or reinforcement learning (RL) loop in your own code while Together runs the GPUs. For the first eight weeks it prices B200 time at $9 per GPU-hour, which Together's account says is down from $11, and it added MiniMax M3.1 Flash as a post-trainable model this week. If you already use the Tinker API, Together says migration is a one-line import change.

The price cut and new model were highlighted on October 29, which is why the story is trending. This post explains what you actually get, what the promo means, and how to judge the vendor's claims.

...

| Question | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| What is it? | A managed service for custom SFT and RL where you define the training loop |
| Price? | $9 per B200 GPU-hour for the first eight weeks (previously $11 in the promo, per Together) |
| Billing unit? | Per GPU-minute on dedicated Model Resources |
| Launch models? | Muse Spark Open, GLM 5.3, Kimi K3, Qwen 3.8-27B; MiniMax M3.1 Flash added |
| Training options? | LoRA (several adapters per GPU allocation) and full-weight for select models |
| Losses? | Cross-entropy, GRPO, CISPO, DPPO, or your own custom objective |
| Migration? | Swap the Tinker import for together.post_training.tinker |
| Customer proof? | Deel, Jack & Jill, Collinear AI, all in Together's own post |

...

## The $9 price in context

Together says the first eight weeks cost $9 per GPU-hour of B200 usage, and its X account describes that as down from $11. Billing is per GPU-minute on dedicated allocations. A few things to keep straight:

- The $9 rate is a promotion with a stated end after eight weeks. The blog post does not give the standard rate afterward, so budget with the pricing page, not the promo.
- Together argues that, thanks to multi-LoRA and dedicated serving optimizations, overall costs fall below token-based pricing as experiments scale. That is a vendor claim; compare it with your own run estimates.
- Several LoRA experiments can share one Model Resource, so a hyperparameter sweep does not need a separate GPU set for each setup.

A rough budget helps. One B200 running for a ten-hour experiment at the promo rate is $90; an eight-GPU allocation for the same ten hours is $720. RL runs with many rollouts can take longer, so size a pilot before committing.

...

Sources: Together Post-Training announcement, Together AI on X, post-training cookbook.

Prices and model availability are as of October 29, 2026. The $9 rate is a limited-time promotion; confirm current pricing with Together.

results.title: How Together AI pricing works: a $15 first credit purchase, GPU clusters from $3.99 an hour, and a $0 balance cut-off that isn't an exact cap | Costbrake
highlights:
### Dedicated inference and GPU clusters

Dedicated single-tenant GPU instances are billed per GPU per hour on demand:

- NVIDIA HGX H100: $5.49 per GPU per hour
- NVIDIA HGX B200: $8.99 per GPU per hour

If you run GPU Clusters, on-demand rates run at $3.99 for NVIDIA HGX H100, $5.99 for H200, $8.19 for B200, and $9.99 for B300 per GPU per hour. If your workloads tolerate interruptions, preemptible compute lowers those hourly rates to $1.99 for H100, $2.99 for H200, $4.09 for B200, and $4.99 for B300. Reserved terms across 3 to 180 days offer deeper discounts; a 91 to 180-day reservation drops an H100 down to $3.19 per hour, an H200 to $3.99, and a B200 to $6.79.

...

### Post-training and fine-tuning

Post-training infrastructure is billed per minute for each active model resource. An NVIDIA HGX B200 costs $11.00 per GPU per hour, discounted to $9.00 per GPU per hour under a promotion valid until 12/14/2026.

results.title: Together Compiler Explained: Speedups, Limits, Availability
results.author: Arafat Shuvo
highlights:
Availability depends on how a team runs its models. For most deployment types, an explainer that read the announcement skeptically couldn't find an answer.

| Deployment or question | What Together has said | Status (Confirmed / Not stated / Unclear) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Serverless endpoints | Already running across many of its most popular serverless endpoints. Customers don't need to change code or settings. | Confirmed |
| Dedicated endpoints | Nothing in the launch materials. | Not stated |
| Fine-tuned or custom models | Nothing on whether customer fine-tunes or uploaded models are retuned. | Not stated |
| Pricing | No price change announced. It isn't clear whether faster kernels will lower list prices or only improve Together's margins. | Unclear |
| "Coming soon" | Coverage uses the phrase but doesn't say which feature, endpoint type, or model it refers to. | Unclear |
| Self-hosted models on a team's own GPUs | Not offered. The system runs inside Together's cloud, so vLLM, SGLang, or TensorRT-LLM deployments don't get it. | Confirmed |

The table reflects launch coverage as of November 5, 2026. Any row marked "Not stated" or "Unclear" should be confirmed with Together before it shapes a budget or migration plan.

# AWS is raising GPU instance prices by ~20% on July 1 — and quietly keeping its own Trainium chips at

Paul Nugent

Nov 4, 2026

AWS is raising GPU instance prices by ~20% on July 1 — and quietly keeping its own Trainium chips at the same price.

This is the most important AI infrastructure pricing story of the year, and the signal is unmistakable.

The move: ~20% price increase on EC2 Capacity Block reservations for Nvidia GPU instances, effective July 1. AWS cited "supply and demand dynamics" — meaning the global compute crunch has gotten severe enough that AWS believes customers will pay more without leaving.

The critical detail: Trainium pricing is unchanged.

AWS now operates two parallel compute economics tracks:

🔹 NVIDIA TRACK: +20% — you absorb Nvidia's pricing power, supply constraints, AND AWS's margin protection layered on top.

🔹 TRAINIUM TRACK: flat — Amazon subsidizes the economics because every workload that migrates to Trainium deepens lock-in to the AWS ecosystem.
